title: Credit Department Standing Basis — Energy Balances Taken Across a Member's Accounts
content:
Credit and contracted gallons are looked at across the member's Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts together.

1. The combined balance is what is owed on every energy account of the member that is not closed, and it is measured against the sum of the limits those accounts carry. Each account's limit is the balance the cooperative will carry on that programme, as the catalogue writes it, and the limits are added across the accounts that go into the combined balance.
2. A delivery is made only where the combined balance after it would stay at or under the combined limit, so a member at their ceiling on the house tank cannot be filled at the dryer instead. What settles this is the standing and the balance the system carries on the accounts, read against the account number before the stop is made; an account admits a delivery while it stands active or past due.
3. Contracted gallons, by contrast, are tied to the account and the fuel they were booked on and are never drawn at another account, because the booking was made against a particular product at a particular price.
4. A payment that names no invoice is applied to the account it was received on, oldest invoice first, and is never spread across accounts.
5. A member who also holds a live grain marketing contract may have their energy balance settled from grain proceeds where the programme allows the transfer, and where it does not, the member pays the energy account directly however the grain settles.

## The same rules put as points of judgement

| Question | What settles it |
| --- | --- |
| Is there room for this stop? | The combined balance after the stop, against the sum of the limits the member's open energy accounts carry |
| May a booking on one account fuel another? | No — contracted gallons stay with the account and the fuel they were booked on |
| Where does an unallocated payment land? | On the account it was received on, oldest invoice first |
| May grain proceeds clear the energy balance? | Only where the programme the account sits on allows the transfer |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical)

A member holds two open energy accounts whose limits add to a combined ceiling. The balance owed across the two, taken after the stop being considered, would land exactly on that ceiling. Because the test is whether the balance would stay at or under the combined limit, landing on it is within the limit and the stop is made. A stop that would carry the combined balance one cent beyond the ceiling is not made, whichever of the two tanks it was to be pumped into.
